name: rtptools
desc: Set of tools for processing RTP data
why: Tools for capturing, replaying and inspecting RTP streams, a direct door into how real-time audio and video travel.

brief.what_it_is: RTP Tools is a set of small command-line applications for processing RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol) data. The README lists six programs: rtpdump parses and prints RTP packets and writes output files that rtpplay and rtpsend can use; rtpplay plays back sessions recorded by rtpdump; rtpsend generates RTP packets from a textual description, written by hand or produced by rtpdump; rtptrans is an RTP translator between unicast and multicast networks; multidump and multiplay start multiple rtpdump or rtpplay instances at once. Recorded or captured RTP goes in, and replayed packets, printed packet details, or translated streams come out.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no separate motivation. It describes the project only as a set of small applications for processing RTP data, and points to the individual manpages for details.
brief.how_it_works: rtpdump turns RTP traffic into a textual or file form that rtpplay and rtpsend can consume, so recording and replaying are a pair of steps. rtpsend builds packets from that textual description. rtptrans relays RTP between unicast and multicast networks. The README does not go deeper into the internals.

commands_seen.context: The usual UNIX build sequence; the README says this should work on any POSIX system.
Autodetects system functions and libraries, producing config.h, config.log and Makefile.local. Re-run after creating configure.local to apply overrides.
Builds the tools once the source is configured. Any POSIX make, BSD or GNU, should work.
Dry run to check where files will be installed before installing.
Installs the binaries and manpages, by default under PREFIX=/usr/local.
Install form when the PREFIX location needs root privileges.
Equivalent install form using doas instead of sudo.

brief.install_notes: On UNIX, run ./configure, then make, then make install. Read config.h, config.log and Makefile.local to check autodetection. If results look wrong, copy configure.local.example to configure.local, set the *DIR variables or other settings there, and run ./configure again. Default PREFIX is /usr/local. On Windows, open rtptools.sln in Microsoft Visual Studio and press F7 to build. Some operating systems ship a prebuilt package, which the README mentions without naming. No accounts or special hardware are mentioned.
brief.standout: The tools are small, separate Unix-style programs that form a record-and-replay pipeline for RTP, with rtpdump's output designed to feed rtpplay and rtpsend. The build uses a hand-rolled autoconf-style configure with small probe programs and compat-*.c fallbacks instead of a package manager.
brief.status: unknown. The README has no release dates, version numbers or changelog, and I did not fetch the commit history or releases page, so I cannot say whether it is actively maintained.
brief.caveats: The README does not include usage examples; it sends readers to the manpages, which I did not fetch. Build failures are possible when headers or libraries are in unusual places, and the README tells users to read config.log to diagnose them. Windows builds use a Visual Studio solution rather than the configure route. No license is stated in the README text I read.
quotes: RTP Tools is a set of small applications that can be used for processing RTP data.
Refer to the individual manpages for details.
RTP tools should compile and run on any POSIX compatible system, as well as on Windows.

judge.reason: A small record, inspect, replay, and generate toolkit makes RTP tangible, offering a hands-on way to learn how real-time audio and video packets travel.

entry.title: rtptools
entry.tldr: Six small Unix programs that record, replay, hand-build and relay RTP streams, the packet format underneath VoIP calls and video conferencing.
entry.deeper_look:
RTP, the Real-time Transport Protocol, is how audio and video usually travel across a network in phone calls and video conferences. rtptools is a set of small command-line programs for handling that traffic. The README describes them as "a set of small applications that can be used for processing RTP data."

The core is a record-and-replay pair. rtpdump parses RTP packets and prints their details, and can also write them to a file. rtpplay plays a recorded session back onto the network. rtpsend takes a textual description of packets, written by hand or produced by rtpdump, and generates real RTP packets from it. multidump and multiplay start several rtpdump or rtpplay instances at once.

The sixth tool, rtptrans, is an RTP translator. It relays a stream between unicast and multicast networks, which is the sort of plumbing a conference system needs when some participants cannot receive multicast.

The idea underneath is that a real-time media stream is just packets you can capture, read as text, edit and send again. Once you can do that, you can see sequence numbers, timestamps and payload types for yourself, and fake a stream without a phone or camera. The README gives no usage examples and sends readers to the individual manpages.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the usage summary for the tool that parses and records RTP packets.
Shows the options for replaying a session recorded by rtpdump.
Shows how to generate RTP packets from a textual description.

entry.whats_unique: It is a small record, edit and replay pipeline for RTP, where rtpdump's output is designed to feed rtpplay and rtpsend. Each tool does one job in the Unix manner.
entry.caveats: The README has no usage examples and no sign of recent activity, so expect to learn from the manpages, and you will need RTP traffic or a hand-written packet description to play with.
